art.title: View of the Cloaca Maxima, Rome
art.why: Ordinary life going on among the ruins of ancient Rome's oldest works (the great drain): the city that took the world, fallen and still lived in.

art.title: The Sanctuary of Hercules
art.why: Armed men kneeling at a pagan shrine: the old gods the pagans said Rome had abandoned.
No NGA Boethius or Philosophy personified.

art.title: Cupid with the Wheel of Time
art.why: An allegory of time's wheel, beside Boethius on eternity and Fortune's wheel.

art.title: A Miracle of Saint Benedict
art.why: Benedict with his monks; the right-hand scene is the rescue of Placidus from the water (Dialogues II.7, not II.1–3: say so). Fra Filippo Lippi's version of the same scene is claimed by monks.

art.title: The Tomb of Caecilia Metella
art.why: A Roman ruin with a shepherd and sheep: the scene of Gibbon's 'decline'.

art.title: Easby Abbey, near Richmond
art.why: A monastery in its landscape. The gallery's description does not mention ruins or monks (only a white building among hills): describe only that. Weak fit: flag.
